blocking_issues: FINDING: class=Necessary. condition=Any overlap window measured with the optional R_A diagnostic path, i.e. OverlapESDInput built with ref_top_carrier/ref_bot_carrier set (the configuration AC-1's response_consistency diagnostic and the Grill-round-3 QC design require). The revised struct gives the ref side ref_top_row0/ref_bot_row0 but no ref-side native_height field, while the binding F2 contract states 'Every carrier evaluation - resample_complex_deramped_reramp, R_A/R_B, any reramp - passes the burst-absolute triple row0/col0/native_height'. A spec-conformant implementation can only evaluate the ref carriers with native_height=None, and both tops_carrier_phase (tops/deramp.py L118) and resample_complex_deramped_reramp (offsets.py L2566) then take centre_row = crop_height//2. path=faninsar/missions/s1 overlap path per Proposed Design esd_overlap.py OverlapESDInput; backed by faninsar/processing/coregistration/tops/deramp.py (carrier_phase_at_points / tops_carrier_phase centre_row fallback) and faninsar/processing/coregistration/offsets.py L2566. impact=For a ~20-line overlap window inside a ~1470-line IW burst the centre_row is wrong by ~725 rows, i.e. eta shifted by ~1.5 s; with TOPS FM rate Kt of ~2.2 kHz/s the carrier frequencies feeding R_A are off by ~3 kHz, the same order as the entire burst-edge Doppler swing that R_B measures. response_consistency = |R_A - R_B| / |R_B| is then O(1)-O(10) on every overlap independent of data quality: the AC-1 per-overlap diagnostic is meaningless and cannot discriminate good from bad overlaps, and any future QC consumption of it is corrupted. This reintroduces, inside the revision's own new struct, the exact omitted-native_height failure class that round-1 F2 closed and that AC-1 ('every carrier evaluation uses the burst-absolute row0/col0/native_height triple') and AC-4 ('omitted or wrong native_height on a crop fails') bind. remedy=Add ref_top_native_height/ref_bot_native_height to OverlapESDInput (or replace the row0/height pairs with a per-carrier (row0, col0, native_height) triplet so ref and sec coordinates cannot silently share), state that for the sec resample native_height is the SECONDARY burst's own full line count (the shipping call at missions/s1/processing.py L2442 already passes the primary's height for the secondary's carrier - the overlap path must not copy that), and extend AC-4 so an R_A evaluation with crop-local centre_row also fails the synthetic regression. claim=Round-1 F2 is not fully closed: the binding triple is unimplementable for the ref-side R_A carrier evaluations as the revised OverlapESDInput is specified. evidence=tops/deramp.py L114-126 and L400-424 (centre_row = n_lines//2 fallback, eta = (row - centre_row)*dt), offsets.py L2566 (same fallback in resample_complex_deramped_reramp), missions/s1/processing.py L2433-2443 (existing call passes primary-burst height with the secondary carrier), stack/session.py L2392-2408 (response_consistency is the only carrier-consistency QC the arc record gets).
advisories: Offset-crop anchoring (optional): the sec resample for a window is only burst-absolute-correct if the azimuth offset crop is taken window-anchored from the FULL-burst geometry field (dense_geometry_offsets row0/col0 semantics, geometry_coreg.py/offsets.py) and the sec deramped input crop starts at the corresponding row of the secondary burst, with the inter-date burst-grid shift absorbed by the offsets. The measure-pass fields computed on the ROI crop (missions/s1/processing.py L1964-1978, L4671-4695) are anchored at the ROI origin and must not be reused for burst-edge windows. Getting this wrong degrades mostly to coherence-gated QC-empty (fail-closed), so it is not blocking, but the design should say 'window-anchored crops of the full-burst geometry+range-Ampcor fields' explicitly.

Lanczos halo at burst-facing window edges (optional): the overlap window sits at the tail of burst i and the head of burst i+1; a window-exact sec crop resampled with lanczos_a=4 plus |azimuth offset| pull cval=0 kernel taps beyond the burst boundary for roughly the last/first (a + |offset|) rows. Those cells lose amplitude and multilook edge cells get a small taper-weighted phase pull; the 0.85 coherence gate plus the coherence-weighted circular mean dilute this below the 0.01 px sigma floor for min_lines=20, but the design should inset each window by (lanczos_a + max|offset| + multilook) rows at the burst-facing edges, mirroring the existing _WINDOW_HALO_FLOOR_PX/_LANCZOS_RADIUS_PX pattern used for ROI crops.

Wrap-range premise (optional, disclosure sharpening): at measurement time the applied azimuth pre-alignment is geometry-only (F3 keeps Ampcor azimuth unapplied and misreg constants out of the measure pass), so the 'residual well under ~0.05 px' premise rests entirely on orbit-based geometry accuracy; a wrapped but coherent overlap yields a confidently wrong small shift that no coherence or spread diagnostic can detect. The Risks section discloses this; make explicit that geometry-only azimuth pre-alignment is the validity premise of the overlap measurer and that the real-S1 NESD magnitude comparison is the check that catches systematic wrap. Relatedly, verification item (c) as worded ('a beyond-wrap shift must never be reported as a small in-wrap value') is unsatisfiable by any measurement-only mechanism for a uniform beyond-wrap shift - per-cell phases all fold to the same value, so there is no spread to flag; restate the pin as: near-wrap shifts are recovered within tolerance, the raw DD phase is surfaced in the record, and beyond-wrap behavior folds exactly as angle() dictates (the confirmed AC-4 wording 'near-wrap and beyond-wrap shifts pinned' is satisfiable; the prose overclaims).

Burst-index and frame alignment (optional): windows are computed from a single S1Swath, so physically adjacent bursts that belong to different SAFE frames (frame boundaries fall on burst edges but the sensing overlap spans the frame cut) are not representable; a selection that only pairs cross-frame bursts yields zero windows and auto silently falls back to split-band. Also, if a secondary date's burst grid is shifted by a whole burst relative to the reference, sec crops pull out-of-burst zeros and the pair degrades to QC-empty fail-closed/auto-fallback rather than a wrong number - acceptable, but worth one sentence in the design. Default burst selection in _burst_kwargs (session.py L1816-1818) is burst 0 only, so out-of-the-box auto runs never exercise overlap; already disclosed in the verification plan, consider a doc note.

Window min_samples (optional): burst_overlap_windows gates on min_lines only; an empty valid-sample range intersection must drop the window entirely, and n_samples below the range multilook (15) needs defined edge behavior. State min_samples (or 'drop windows with n_samples < range multilook') in the window contract.

Sigma plumbing (optional): the forced-residual seam (missions/s1/processing.py L2052-2055) sets only esd_azimuth_shift_px per unit; the aggregate sigma lives in the consensus scope. The design's 'arcs read state.esd_azimuth_shift_px + state.esd_sigma_px' requires the aggregate sigma to be written onto the pair-level state that _produce_pair returns (origin_state via _inherit_coregistration_residuals), not only onto per-burst worker states; one sentence in the design closes this.

Split-band fallback zero-shift (optional, pre-existing): when auto falls back on QC-empty, the split-band estimator itself returns ESDResult(0.0, 0.0, 0.0) on total decorrelation (esd.py L180-189) and measure_misreg turns None into 0.0 arcs with sigma 1.0 (session.py L2392, L2404). That is unchanged split-band behavior outside this proposal's scope, but the Risks sentence 'with no qualifying samples the arc is not emitted (fail-closed) rather than defaulted to zero' is true only for the explicit-overlap fail-closed cases; scope that sentence to them.
